attempts.raw_response: The second structure, completed in 1906, remains a vital railway link. It features a robust steel truss design that reflects the engineering standards of the early twentieth century, prioritizing durability and load-bearing capacity for heavy freight trains traversing the rugged terrain of Norrland. The third bridge, constructed in 1975, represents modern concrete technology. This prestressed concrete span offers greater efficiency and lower maintenance costs compared to its predecessors. Together, these three distinct structures form a unique architectural timeline. They illustrate the technological evolution from iron to steel, and finally to reinforced concrete. Visitors can appreciate this historical progression by walking along the old road bridge or observing the newer spans from nearby viewpoints. The site serves as an open-air museum of civil engineering achievements.

pair.human_continuation:
The concrete bridge from 1919 has been declared a historic monument.

The first bridge was built to allow the rail line to head north; it is made of steel and is 180m long (it is now a road bridge). As the power of steam locomotives increased, a sturdier bridge was needed. A reinforced concrete structure was built in 1919, 140m downstream, towering 90m over the river. The third and final bridge was built of steel and concrete, opening in 1994. It is 338m long, the longest bridge on the rail line.

1891 Bridge
This bridge is a steel truss bridge, with four suspended parabolic trusses (each of a different length), for a total span of 164m. It now serves as the road bridge over the river.
pair.prefix:
The  Tallberg Bridges  (Tallbergsbroarna in Swedish) consist of three railway bridges that cross the Öre River at Slätforsen, about 4 km from Nyåker, Nordmaling Municipality in Sweden. They are part of the Northern Main Line through upper Norrland. One of the bridges has been rebuilt for road traffic. The three bridges show how bridge construction has changed over the course of a century.

Details
The oldest bridge is a steel truss bridge built in 1891, now a road bridge.
